lessons.title: How do you feel?
lessons.goal: Talk about your feelings and react to other people's news.

tip.title: Reflexive verbs
tip.body: Many feeling verbs are reflexive: sich freuen, sich ärgern, sich fühlen. The pronoun matches the subject: ich freue mich, du freust dich, wir freuen uns. Sich freuen auf means to look forward to; sich freuen über means to be happy about. To sound empathetic, let your voice fall gently on "Das tut mir leid".

lessons.title: Friends and partners
lessons.goal: Describe people close to you and how your relationships developed.

tip.title: Relative clauses
tip.body: Describe people with relative clauses: Das ist die Freundin, die in Wien wohnt. Der Freund, den ich getroffen habe, ist Lehrer. The relative pronoun matches the person's gender and its role in the clause, and the verb goes to the end. Fluency tip: one relative clause per sentence is plenty when speaking.

lessons.title: Comfort and encouragement
lessons.goal: Show sympathy and encourage someone who is having a hard time.

tip.title: Showing empathy
tip.body: Short reactions show you are listening: Oh nein! Echt? Das verstehe ich. To cheer someone up, say Kopf hoch! (literally "head up") or Das schaffst du schon. Speak a little more slowly and softly than usual.

lessons.title: Worauf? Darauf! — da- and wo- words
lessons.goal: Ask and answer with verbs that take a fixed preposition.

tip.title: wo(r)- to ask, da(r)- to answer
tip.body: Many feeling verbs have a fixed preposition: sich freuen auf, sich ärgern über, Angst haben vor, denken an. For things, ask with wo + preposition (Worauf freust du dich?) and refer back with da + preposition (Ich freue mich darauf); add -r- before a vowel. For people, keep preposition + pronoun: Auf wen wartest du?

lessons.title: Joys, worries and wishes
lessons.goal: Talk about what makes you happy, what annoys you and what you wish for.

culture.title: Friends through the Verein
culture.body: Clubs (Vereine) are a big part of social life in German-speaking countries: sports clubs, choirs, volunteer fire brigades, allotment and carnival clubs. Many adults make their closest friends there rather than at work. Joining a Verein is one of the best ways to meet locals and practise German.
